vocabulary.example: Do you have a bigger size?
I like it. I'll take it.

grammar.explanation_en: 'This' and 'these' point to things near you (this = singular, these = plural). 'That' and 'those' point to things far away (that = singular, those = plural). They are very useful when shopping and pointing at items.
grammar.explanation_ko: 'this'와 'these'는 가까이 있는 것을 가리키고(this = 단수, these = 복수), 'that'과 'those'는 멀리 있는 것을 가리킵니다(that = 단수, those = 복수). 쇼핑할 때 물건을 가리키며 말할 때 아주 유용합니다.

examples.en: Those shoes over there are nice.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: Excuse me, how much is this jacket?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: It's 50 dollars. Do you like the color?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: Yes! Do you have a bigger size?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: Yes, here you are. I'll take it!

reading.title: A Trip to the Market
reading.text: I went to the market today. I saw a nice hat. I asked, 'How much is this hat?' The seller said, 'It's ten dollars.' It was cheap, so I said, 'I'll take it!' I also bought some cheap fruit.
reading.text_ko: 오늘 시장에 갔어요. 예쁜 모자를 봤어요. 'ㅇ이 모자 얼마예요?'라고 물어봤어요. 판매자는 '10달러예요.'라고 했어요. 저렴해서 '이걸로 살게요!'라고 했어요. 저렴한 과일도 좀 샀어요.

explanation.en: The text says 'It was cheap, so I said, I'll take it!'
The text says 'I also bought some cheap fruit.'
explanation.ko: 본문에 'I also bought some cheap fruit.'이라고 나옵니다.
